props.title: Which act fits which kind of event?
props.lede: Most people book by the kind of event first and the sound second, so here’s the roster sorted that way.

rows.term: A cocktail hour, a dinner, or background music
rows.text: For a cocktail hour or a dinner, a solo guitarist, a singer and guitarist, a Spanish guitarist, a jazz duo, an acoustic duo or a pianist can all play at a volume your guests can talk across. Last Consulate (one musician on upright bass and guitar over downtempo electronics) is a great choice when you want something a little more modern. In December the Christmas jazz trio plays the season’s songs at the same volume.

rows.term: A party with a dance floor
rows.text: A trio or a quartet is the size to book when you want people dancing. Tejas Singh and Tony Medina can both start small and grow to a four piece over the evening, and the Americana band, the yacht rock band, the soul and R&B band and the funk band each get people dancing to a different sound. Live band karaoke is the one where your guests take the mic.

rows.term: A DJ, on its own or after the band
rows.text: The DJ is open format, and can play the whole night or take over after any band on the roster through the same sound system.

rows.term: A set piece your guests watch
rows.text: When you want something your guests will stop and watch, book Dirty Flamenco, Changes Jazz Trio with a saxophone added, or René Moffatt playing his own songs. Your Bird Can Sing gets a whole crowd singing along, and Firstwater plays a sound bath at an offsite or a wellness day.

Many couples book an acoustic or Spanish guitarist for the ceremony, a duo for the cocktail hour and the DJ for the dance floor. A wedding jazz band can cover the whole day in one style. Find out more on our weddings page.

A jazz duo or a guitarist works well for senior living, a memorial or a Sunday brunch, the Beatles sing-along is a great choice for a community afternoon, and a sound bath can be booked during the day too. Find out more on our daytime page.

props.html: Every act plays Denver, the Front Range and the mountain towns. Our pricing page has a general view of what live music costs in Denver and Colorado.

props._notes:
Two lanes, 2026-09-23. The roster grid used to list every act in file
     order, named and spec'd mixed, with the hand-typed configuration index
     fourteen phone screens further down and five configuration pages that
     were on no card at all. Now the configurations come first, compact and
     smallest first, and the named acts follow with their footage. Both lanes
     render from acts.json (`lane`, see its _lanes_note), so a new act joins
     the right lane on the next build with nothing to type here.

     Filter UI ships hidden and acts.js unhides it, so with script off every
     act on the roster is still on the page. The filter is a class toggle
     over data attributes rendered by build.py, never a re-render, and it
     works across both lanes; a lane with nothing left in it hides its own
     heading. The page opens pre-filtered from a query string
     (?occasion=weddings, ?size=duo, ?genre=jazz, ?night=party), which is how
     an occasion page can point at the acts that suit it.

Daniel's disclaimer, 2026-09-19, on the page that lists every act and
         size. The footer carries the same sentence sitewide.

props.html: Stage lighting and a dedicated engineer are optional add-ons. Travel outside the metro, holiday weekends and New Year's Eve are also available as market priced.
Want to know more? The full FAQ list covers everything from substitutions to volume limits.

items.q: What's the difference between a "named act" and a configuration?
items.a: A named act, like Tejas Singh or Dirty Flamenco, is booked under its own name, so you know exactly who is playing. A format, like a jazz duo or a yacht rock band, is played by professional musicians we match to your date and your venue. Either one can be booked by sending us the date.

Denver, Boulder, Colorado Springs and Fort Collins, and the mountain towns: Vail, Beaver Creek, Aspen, Breckenridge, Telluride, Steamboat Springs, Winter Park and Crested Butte. For a venue outside the Denver metro area, just let us know where it is and we can price the travel with the date.
